model_card_fields.params: Parameter count as written by the authors, e.g. "51M" or "3B"; or counted from the released weights, marked "(counted from released weights)".
model_card_fields.pretraining_cells: Number of cells in the pretraining corpus, e.g. "33M".
model_card_fields.pretraining_data: Corpus name and version, e.g. "CELLxGENE Census 2023-05-15".
model_card_fields.tokenization: e.g. rank, binning, value-projection, protein-embedding, text.
model_card_fields.license: Licence of code/weights, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0.

inputs.label: Gene expression
inputs.desc: Gene expression counts or profiles (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, bulk).

inputs.label: Protein abundance
inputs.desc: CITE-seq antibody counts, cytometry or proteomics measurements.

inputs.label: Spatial coordinates
inputs.desc: Cell or spot positions, or spatial neighbourhoods.

inputs.label: Cell image
inputs.desc: Microscopy, Cell Painting or protein-localisation images.

inputs.label: Protein sequence
inputs.desc: Amino-acid sequences or protein language model inputs.

inputs.label: Text
inputs.desc: Natural language: metadata, descriptions or questions.

inputs.label: Perturbation
inputs.desc: Identity of a genetic or chemical perturbation.

inputs.label: Prior network
inputs.desc: A given graph: gene regulatory network, protein interactions, pathways or a knowledge graph.

outputs.label: Disease state
outputs.desc: Disease or condition status of cells or donors.

outputs.label: Expression prediction
outputs.desc: Imputation, denoising or cross-modality translation of measurements.

outputs.label: Perturbation response
outputs.desc: Predicted effect of a genetic or chemical perturbation.

outputs.label: Gene prioritization
outputs.desc: Ranked genes, such as drivers, key regulators or therapeutic targets.

architecture_families.label: Transformer encoder-decoder
architecture_families.desc: Separate encoder and decoder, including asymmetric designs.

architecture_families.label: State-space model
architecture_families.desc: Mamba, Hyena and similar long-sequence models.

architecture_families.label: Graph neural network
architecture_families.desc: Message passing over cell or gene graphs.

architecture_families.label: Diffusion model
architecture_families.desc: Denoising diffusion, including latent and discrete diffusion.

architecture_families.label: Large language model
architecture_families.desc: A fine-tuned or prompted general-purpose LLM.

architecture_families.label: Agent system
architecture_families.desc: One or more LLM agents with tools.

architecture_families.label: Other
architecture_families.desc: None of the above; the free-text `architecture` field says what.

code_status.label: No code found
code_status.desc: Searched the paper, GitHub and Hugging Face; nothing public.

code_status.label: Release pending

interp_methods.label: Sparse autoencoder
interp_methods.desc: Decomposes activations into sparse, interpretable features.

interp_methods.label: Circuit tracing
interp_methods.desc: Ablates or patches features to map causal paths inside the model (incl. transcoders).

interp_methods.label: Attention analysis
interp_methods.desc: Reads or ablates attention weights and heads.

interp_methods.label: Probing
interp_methods.desc: Trains simple read-outs on frozen representations.

interp_methods.label: Attribution
interp_methods.desc: Gradient or perturbation scores of input-gene importance.

interp_methods.label: Representation geometry
interp_methods.desc: Spectral, topological or subspace analysis of embeddings.

review_basis.label: Metadata
review_basis.desc: Title, venue, year and links checked against Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv or bioRxiv.

review_basis.label: Abstract
review_basis.desc: Fields read from the paper's abstract.

review_basis.label: Repository
review_basis.desc: Checked against the code repository or model card.

models.key: BERT-style model that bins gene expression values into categories; used for cell-type annotation.

resources.title: A genome-scale single-cell CRISPRi map of trans gene regulation across human pluripotent stem cell lines
resources.citation: Feng, Claudia, Elin Madli Peets, Yan Zhou, Luca Crepaldi, Sunay Usluer, Alistair Dunham, Jana M. Braunger et al. "A genome-scale single-cell CRISPRi map of trans gene regulation across human pluripotent stem cell lines." Cell Genomics 6, no. 2 (2026): 101076.

resources.title: A leakage-aware benchmark for evaluating chemical and cellular generalization in single-cell perturbation-response prediction
resources.key: Leakage-aware splits that separate chemical-analogue, new-scaffold, new-context and new-mechanism generalisation for perturbation models.
resources.findings: Reported performance depends strongly on the split; scaffold splits still leave many same-mechanism neighbours.
resources.citation: Lin, Da, Ying Chen, Yue Liu, and Yu Zhang. "A leakage-aware benchmark for evaluating chemical and cellular generalization in single-cell perturbation-response prediction." Research Square (2026).

resources.title: A mechanism-annotated benchmark reveals limited fidelity to drug-response signatures in single-cell perturbation models
resources.key: scDrugPerturb-Bench: links drug perturbation profiles to curated drug-response signatures to test mechanism fidelity, not just reconstruction.
resources.findings: Models show limited fidelity to drug-response signatures; good reconstruction is a poor proxy, and frozen FM embeddings give only local gains.
resources.citation: Li, Lehang, Shaoming Duan, Xinyu Zha, Ye Fang, Yuhao Zhang, Xinyi Zhang, Yang Cao et al. "A mechanism-annotated benchmark reveals limited fidelity to drug-response signatures in single-cell perturbation models." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: A Standardized Framework For Evaluating Gene Expression Generative Models
resources.key: GGE: open-source framework of standardised distributional and DEG-focused metrics for single-cell generative models.
resources.findings: Metric values vary substantially with implementation choices, so standardised reporting is needed.
resources.citation: Rubbi, Andrea, Andrea Giuseppe Di Francesco, Mohammad Lotfollahi, and Pietro Liò. "A Standardized Framework For Evaluating Gene Expression Generative Models." arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.11244 (2026).

resources.title: A systematic assessment of single-cell language model configurations
resources.key: bento-sc: isolates pretraining choices of single-cell language models one at a time to find which design decisions matter.
resources.findings: scLMs do not yet beat baselines by much; best results come from minimally processed counts, count-distribution losses, high masking rates and combined objectives.
resources.citation: Waele, Gaetan De, Gerben Menschaert, and Willem Waegeman. "A systematic assessment of single-cell language model configurations." NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 8, no. 3 (2026).

resources.title: A Systematic Comparison of Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction Models
resources.findings: PerturbNet best recovers DE signatures, but no method generalises across cell types; fine-tuned foundation models underestimate synergy.
resources.citation: Li, Lanxiang, Yue You, Yunlin Fu, Wenyu Liao, Xueying Fan, Shihong Lu, Ye Cao et al. "A systematic comparison of single-cell perturbation response prediction models." Science Advances 12, no. 37 (2026): eaed3414.

resources.title: A world model of the virtual cell
resources.key: Proposes the virtual cell world model: a stateful system that simulates a cell's evolution under interventions, with an architecture, data and evaluation plan.
resources.citation: Xing, Eric P., and Le Song. "A world model of the virtual cell." Cell 189, no. 19 (2026): 5831-5844.

resources.title: Accessible and reproducible deployment reveals the practical boundaries of single-cell foundation models
resources.findings: Usefulness is neither universal nor set by model scale; it depends on the representation, the biological context and the supervision.
resources.citation: Hou, Siyu, Penghui Yang, Wenjing Ma, Jinxi Xiang, Jade Xiaoqing Wang, Hui Wan, Ying Ma et al. "Accessible and reproducible deployment reveals the practical boundaries of single-cell foundation models." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: AmbiModBench: Benchmarking Gene Perturbation Prediction Beyond Shared Responses
resources.key: AmbiModBench: specificity-aware perturbation benchmark that separates target-specific predictions from shared background responses.
resources.findings: Strong absolute scores mostly reflect the shared background response rather than target-specific learning.
resources.citation: Huang, Sikai, Zhiwen Yang, Kai Yu, Jiayuan Chen, and Stan Z. Li. "AmbiModBench: Benchmarking Gene Perturbation Prediction Beyond Shared Responses." arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.32527 (2026).

resources.title: An Empirical Comparison of Virtual Cell Models: Perturbation Prediction, Representation, and the Baseline Gap
resources.key: Compares perturbation predictors, foundation-model embeddings and STATE on prediction and representation tasks against linear baselines.
resources.findings: Deep models gain on combinatorial perturbations, unseen cell types and especially representation tasks, but rarely beat baselines on perturbation prediction.
resources.citation: Denvis, Olivia. "An Empirical Comparison of Virtual Cell Models: Perturbation Prediction, Representation, and the Baseline Gap." Research Square (2026).

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence Virtual Organoids (AIVOs)
resources.key: Review defining AI virtual organoids: organoid-scale digital twins built from virtual cells, with architecture, construction, evaluation and applications.
resources.citation: Bai, Long, and Jiacan Su. "Artificial Intelligence Virtual Organoids (AIVOs)." Bioactive Materials 59 (2026): 45-68.

resources.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled multi-scale virtual cell: perspective, challenges, and opportunities
resources.citation: Jiang, Huasen, et al. "Artificial intelligence-enabled multi-scale virtual cell: perspective, challenges, and opportunities." Briefings in Bioinformatics 27.2 (2026): bbag104.

resources.title: AssayBench: An Assay-Level Virtual Cell Benchmark for LLMs and Agents
resources.findings: General-purpose LLMs used zero-shot beat biology-specific models and agents, but every method stays well below the estimated performance ceiling.
resources.citation: De Brouwer, Edward, Carl Edwards, Alexander Wu, Jenna Collier, Graham Heimberg, Xiner Li, Meena Subramaniam et al. "AssayBench: An Assay-Level Virtual Cell Benchmark for LLMs and Agents." arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.10876 (2026).

resources.title: Assessing scale and predictive diversity in models for single-cell transcriptomics based on Geneformer
resources.key: Studies architecture and pretraining scale for Geneformer-style rank-based models (GF-CAB).
resources.findings: More pretraining data does not uniformly help; models trained on much less data can match or beat larger ones.
resources.citation: Chen, Junfan, Fabian Schmidt, and Ricardo Henao. "Assessing scale and predictive diversity in models for single-cell transcriptomics based on Geneformer." PLOS Computational Biology 22, no. 7 (2026): e1013701.

resources.title: Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models
resources.key: Audits uncertainty-calibrated benchmarking of perturbation models (scVI, CPA, ridge) and documents six failure modes.
resources.findings: Marginal coverage can look fine while covering few DE-gene intervals; conformal prediction should be recalibrated per context.
resources.citation: Gallone, Manuel, Shyam Ravidath, and Srihith Madireddy. "Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Auditing pretraining contamination in single-cell foundation model benchmarks
resources.key: scContam: audits whether benchmark cells were in foundation-model pretraining data, at the cell level.
resources.findings: Models resist memorising individual cells, but contaminated cells embed measurably more tightly, so pretraining audits should accompany benchmarks.
resources.citation: Ali, Sarwan. "Auditing pretraining contamination in single-cell foundation model benchmarks." arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.20572 (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction
resources.key: Compares biological knowledge-graph priors with single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
resources.citation: Ni, Jie, Xinting Zhang, Mingyang Li, Yuhan Cai, Zhuoying Xie, and Yun Liu. "Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction." Computational Biology and Chemistry 126 (2026): 109480.

resources.title: Benchmarking gene expression reconstruction from single-cell latent representations
resources.key: ReconEval: benchmarks how well gene expression can be decoded back from latent spaces, from PCA and autoencoders to frozen foundation-model embeddings.
resources.findings: Autoencoders reconstruct best at low dimension; frozen foundation-model embeddings keep recoverable gene information, but high-dimensional PCA matches them for latent perturbation modelling.
resources.citation: Fu, Xiaotong, Dominik Klein, Egor Antipov, Alessandro Palma, Alejandro Tejada-Lapuerta, Mojtaba Bahrami, Louis B. Kummerle et al. "Benchmarking gene expression reconstruction from single-cell latent representations." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking LLM-based agents for single-cell omics analysis
resources.key: Benchmark of LLM-based agent frameworks on single-cell omics analysis tasks across omics types, species and technologies.
resources.findings: Multi-agent frameworks beat single agents; code quality matters most, and self-reflection helps more than retrieval or planning.
resources.citation: Liu, Yang, Lu Zhou, Xiawei Du, Ruikun He, Xuguang Zhang, Rongbo Shen, and Yixue Li. "Benchmarking LLM-based agents for single-cell omics analysis." Genome Biology 27, no. 1 (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models for real-world RNA-seq data integration
resources.key: Benchmarks foundation models against scVI and Harmony for integrating 1.5M clinical and preclinical cells, with robustness rankings.
resources.findings: Fine-tuning helps, but scVI is the best overall integrator.
resources.citation: Han, Siyu, Tamas Sztanka-Toth, Enes Senel, Ahmed Elnaggar, Jaymala Patel, Tommaso Mansi, Denis Smirnov et al. "Benchmarking single-cell foundation models for real-world RNA-seq data integration." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models in a zero-shot setting
resources.key: Zero-shot evaluation of four foundation models on annotation, protein-expression prediction and integration.
resources.findings: Baselines win most annotation and integration tasks; foundation embeddings help for protein prediction (SCimilarity, TranscriptFormer).
resources.citation: Gaballa, Yasmine, Somaia Ahmed, and Tamim Abdelaal. "Benchmarking single-cell foundation models in a zero-shot setting." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
resources.key: Benchmarks four foundation-model representations on 868 disease-prediction and 65 cell-type tasks from CELLxGENE.
resources.findings: With full data, log-normalised counts match or beat the best model; with about 100 labelled cells per class or fewer, TranscriptFormer wins.
resources.citation: Benhayon, Haya, Michael M. Danziger, Danny Ben-Zvi, and Michal Rosen-Zvi. "Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking Static Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction and Dynamic Transition Probing in Single-Cell Foundation Models
resources.key: Benchmarks regulatory networks recovered from token embeddings, hidden states and attention of six foundation models, and adds dynamic transition probing.
resources.findings: scGPT token embeddings beat classical GRN baselines and scFoundation best reproduces developmental transitions; what can be recovered depends on architecture and extraction.
resources.citation: Ye, Zhongni, Ning Yang, Xiaojing Yang, Xiaowei Mao, and Chao Tang. "Benchmarking Static Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction and Dynamic Transition Probing in Single-Cell Foundation Models." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking virtual cell models for in-the-wild perturbation response
resources.key: Standardized, modular benchmark for virtual cell perturbation prediction under unseen cell contexts, unseen perturbations, and cross-dataset generalization; finds performance is highly context-dependent and often overestimated in standard setups.
resources.findings: Performance is often overestimated and drops sharply under stricter context shifts; models capture global trends but miss perturbation-specific effects.
resources.citation: Mao, Xinjie, Songming Zhang, Qianhong Wen, Xiangyu Wen, Kedu Jin, Hao Wu, Shuizhou Chen, Yuqiang Li, Lei Bai, Qi Liu, Ning Ding, Siqi Sun, and Zhangyang Gao. "Benchmarking virtual cell models for in-the-wild perturbation response." arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.27646 (2026).

resources.title: Benchmarking zero-shot single-cell foundation model embeddings for cellular dynamics reconstruction
resources.key: Benchmarks zero-shot foundation-model embeddings for reconstructing trajectories from time-resolved single-cell data.
resources.findings: The HVG baseline beats foundation embeddings; the models over-compress temporal signal and flatten branches.
resources.citation: Zhou, Xueya, Zihan Wang, Yue Ling, Qinxue Tian, Zhenyi Zhang, Yongge Li, Luonan Chen et al. "Benchmarking zero-shot single-cell foundation model embeddings for cellular dynamics reconstruction." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Beyond Expression Prediction: Benchmarking Differential Expression Classification in Single-Cell Perturbation Models
resources.key: Evaluates perturbation models on predicting differential-expression outcomes for unseen perturbations and unseen cell lines.
resources.findings: Simple baselines like embedding nearest neighbours are competitive or better; sparsity calibration helps deep models.
resources.citation: Sun, Junwei, Yuxun He, Ouyang Zhu, and Yiqun T. Chen. "Beyond Expression Prediction: Benchmarking Differential Expression Classification in Single-Cell Perturbation Models." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Beyond the Final Layer: Evaluating Single-Cell Foundation Model Representations for Molecular Prediction
resources.key: Layer-wise probing of four foundation models as frozen feature extractors for cell-type and perturbation prediction, with readout and geometry diagnostics.
resources.findings: Intermediate layers often beat the final layer for scGPT and scBERT cell-type tasks; the best depth depends on model, task and readout.
resources.citation: Wen, Ming-Ching Crystal, YiWei Lyu, and Andrew Robbins. "Beyond the Final Layer: Evaluating Single-Cell Foundation Model Representations for Molecular Prediction." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Can We Trust In-Distribution Success? Locked Evaluation Reveals Transfer Failure and Sampling-Depth Entanglement in CRISPRi Perturbation Prediction
resources.key: Pre-registered, locked evaluation of a frozen Geneformer representation for CRISPRi perturbation-effect prediction.
resources.findings: In-distribution success does not transfer, and the challenge endpoint is strongly tied to cell count.
resources.citation: Shoeibi, Mehrdad, and Niloofar Yousefi. "Can We Trust In-Distribution Success? Locked Evaluation Reveals Transfer Failure and Sampling-Depth Entanglement in CRISPRi Perturbation Prediction." arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.00152 (2026).

resources.title: Causal circuit tracing reveals distinct computational architectures in single-cell foundation models: inhibitory dominance, biological coherence, and cross-model convergence
resources.key: Ablates sparse-autoencoder features one at a time in Geneformer and scGPT to map model-internal causal circuits and compares them with known regulation.
resources.findings: The circuits are reproducible and enriched for known biology and ChIP-seq-supported TF targets, but largely mirror co-expression.
resources.citation: Kendiukhov, Ihor. "Causal circuit tracing reveals distinct computational architectures in single-cell foundation models: inhibitory dominance, biological coherence, and cross-model convergence." Bioinformatics 42, no. 7 (2026): btag379.

resources.title: Causal intervention validation of gene regulatory signals in scGPT
resources.key: Ablates or swaps transcription-factor tokens inside scGPT, traces circuits with activation patching, and checks the resulting edges against curated references and CRISPR data.
resources.citation: Kendiukhov, Ihor. "Causal intervention validation of gene regulatory signals in scGPT." Journal of Biomedical Informatics 180 (2026): 105080.

resources.title: Cell shapes decode molecular phenotypes in image-based spatial proteomics
resources.citation: Le, Trang, William D. Leineweber, Matheus P. Viana, Anthony Cesnik, Jan N. Hansen, Wei Ouyang, Susanne M. Rafelski et al. "Cell shapes decode molecular phenotypes in image-based spatial proteomics." Cell Systems 17, no. 6 (2026): 101589.

resources.title: CLAMP: Steady-State ODE Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell Perturbations
resources.venue_detail: Workshop on Generative and Agentic AI for Biology
resources.key: Fits one shared steady-state ODE to Perturb-seq data through a frozen foundation-model encoder, so recovery of the regulatory network measures how much regulatory structure the encoder keeps.
resources.findings: Each foundation-model encoder loses regulatory structure in its own way: some cannot keep regulatory directions separable, others keep them only non-linearly.
resources.citation: Gallagher-Syed, Amaya, Aaron Wenteler, Santiago A. Martinez, and Gregory Slabaugh. "CLAMP: Steady-State ODE Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell Perturbations." In Workshop on Generative and Agentic AI for Biology at ICML (2026).

resources.title: Context-dependent utility and robustness of pretrained single-cell foundation model representations across analytical tasks
resources.key: Zero-shot evaluation of 20 representation methods on 6 tasks and 1,607 datasets, testing both utility and robustness to changes in dataset structure.
resources.findings: No method wins across tasks, top performers are often fragile to dataset changes, and simple statistical methods stay competitive.
resources.citation: Liu, Tianyuan, Tingze Feng, Xianrun Pan, Yangyang Chen, Liping Ren, Xiucai Ye, Hao Lin, and Yang Zhang. "Context-dependent utility and robustness of pretrained single-cell foundation model representations across analytical tasks." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Decoding Conserved and Tissue-Specific Cellular Stress Programs from Single-Cell Foundation Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
resources.key: Uses sparse autoencoders on foundation-model embeddings of a multi-organ ageing atlas to extract cellular stress programs.
resources.findings: The features recover known and new stress programs, some conserved across tissues and increasingly co-active with age, others tissue-specific.
resources.citation: Bashir, Abdul. "Decoding Conserved and Tissue-Specific Cellular Stress Programs from Single-Cell Foundation Models Using Sparse Autoencoders." ScienceOpen Preprints (2026).

resources.title: Discovery of a Hematopoietic Manifold in scGPT Yields a Method for Extracting Performant Algorithms from Biological Foundation Model Internals
resources.key: Finds a hematopoietic manifold inside scGPT and exports it from frozen attention weights as a compact standalone algorithm.
resources.findings: The extracted algorithm orders pseudotime best against scVI, Palantir and others, with about 1000-fold fewer trainable parameters than probing.
resources.citation: Kendiukhov, Ihor. "Discovery of a Hematopoietic Manifold in scGPT Yields a Method for Extracting Performant Algorithms from Biological Foundation Model Internals." arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.10261 (2026).

resources.title: Dissecting the Virtual Cell: A Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Single-cell Biological Foundation Models
resources.key: Review of mechanistic interpretability methods applied to single-cell foundation models.
resources.citation: Denvis, Olivia. "Dissecting the Virtual Cell: A Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Single-cell Biological Foundation Models." SSRN (2026).

resources.title: Do Geometric Outliers Identify Important Genes in Single-Cell Foundation Models?
resources.key: Screens Geneformer, scGPT and scFoundation gene embeddings for geometric outliers and tests whether those genes matter for annotation or disease.
resources.findings: The models agree only weakly on outlier genes, and outliers neither drive cell-type annotation nor mark disease genes; embedding geometry is mostly model-specific.
resources.citation: Whalley, Justin P. "Do Geometric Outliers Identify Important Genes in Single-Cell Foundation Models?" bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Evaluating Single-Cell Perturbation Response Models Is Far from Straightforward
resources.key: Stress-tests perturbation models and their metrics with cross-splitting, controlled noise and synthetic data.
resources.findings: Common correlation and distribution metrics are swayed by scale, sparsity and dimension; complex models often trail simple baselines on chemical perturbation data.
resources.citation: Heidari, Mahshid, Mina Karimpour, Sumana Srivatsa, and Hesam Montazeri. "Evaluating Single-Cell Perturbation Response Models Is Far from Straightforward." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation
resources.key: SAFFRON: uses Matryoshka sparse autoencoders on spatial foundation-model embeddings to test whether they capture local and global spatial variation.
resources.findings: Novae captures global spatial gradients better than simple baselines, but no spatial model beats baselines on local microenvironment patterns.
resources.citation: Handa, Dhanav, Cristina Martin-Linares, Genevieve Stein-O’Brien, Jonathan Ling, and Uthsav Chitra. "Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Evaluating the learnability of single-cell large language models on multiple tasks
resources.key: Tests whether larger models and more data help Geneformer and scGPT on perturbation prediction and annotation, using real and synthetic data.
resources.findings: Scaling gives little or even hurts; for perturbation prediction the models seem to capture little beyond summary statistics.
resources.citation: Yan, Yu, Xutao Wang, and Dongyuan Song. "Evaluating the learnability of single-cell large language models on multiple tasks." BMC Genomics 27, no. 1 (2026).

resources.title: Evaluating the role of pretraining dataset size and diversity on single-cell foundation model performance
resources.findings: Performance plateaus with a fraction of current corpora; there are no clear data scaling laws.
resources.citation: DenAdel, Alan, Madeline Hughes, Akshaya Thoutam, Anay Gupta, Andrew W. Navia, Nicolo Fusi, Srivatsan Raghavan et al. "Evaluating the role of pretraining dataset size and diversity on single-cell foundation model performance." Nature Methods 23, no. 7 (2026): 1447-1457.

resources.title: Evaluating the utilities of foundation models in single-cell data analysis
resources.findings: Foundation models do not consistently beat task-specific methods; scGPT, Geneformer and CellFM come out on top.
resources.citation: Liu, Tianyu, Kexing Li, Yuge Wang, Hongyu Li, and Hongyu Zhao. "Evaluating the Utilities of Foundation Models in Single‐Cell Data Analysis." Advanced Science 13, no. 27 (2026): e14490.

resources.title: Evaluation protocol choices dominate reported performance in gene regulatory network benchmarks for single-cell foundation models
resources.key: Decomposes GRN evaluation for scGPT attention networks into symbol mapping, gold standard, candidate set and label noise.
resources.findings: Protocol choices shift AUPR by orders of magnitude; under universe-aware scoring scGPT attention falls below random, while GENIE3 and GRNBoost2 do better.
resources.citation: Kendiukhov, Ihor. "Evaluation protocol choices dominate reported performance in gene regulatory network benchmarks for single-cell foundation models." Research Square (2026).

resources.title: Exhaustive Circuit Mapping of a Single-Cell Foundation Model Reveals Massive Redundancy, Heavy-Tailed Hub Architecture, and Layer-Dependent Differentiation Control
resources.key: Traces every active sparse-autoencoder feature in one Geneformer layer, tests higher-order ablations and steers cell trajectories with features.
resources.findings: Exhaustive tracing reveals a heavy-tailed hub structure missed by selective sampling and strong redundancy; late-layer features push cells toward maturity.
resources.citation: Kendiukhov, Ihor. "Exhaustive Circuit Mapping of a Single-Cell Foundation Model Reveals Massive Redundancy, Heavy-Tailed Hub Architecture, and Layer-Dependent Differentiation Control." arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.11940 (2026).

resources.title: Fifteen challenges for generative AI applications to cell biology
resources.key: Fifteen grand challenges, modelled on Hilbert's problems, for generative AI in cell biology.
resources.citation: Dupire, Leo, Aly A. Khan, Theofanis Karaletsos, Shana Kelley, Emma Lundberg, Jian Ma, Evan Paull et al. "Fifteen challenges for generative AI applications to cell biology." Cell 189, no. 19 (2026): 5870-5892.

resources.title: Foundation Models for Single-cell Biology: A Review of Architectures, Benchmarks, and the Push toward Mechanistic Understanding
resources.key: Review of single-cell foundation model architectures and benchmarks, and of the move toward mechanistic understanding.
resources.citation: Denvis, Olivia. "Foundation Models for Single-cell Biology: A Review of Architectures, Benchmarks, and the Push toward Mechanistic Understanding." SSRN (2026).

aliases: Foundation Models Improve Perturbation Response Prediction
resources.title: Foundation models improve perturbation response prediction
resources.key: Compares 600+ models for embedding-based perturbation response prediction; some foundation models beat simple baselines, and combining several helps.
resources.citation: Cole, Elijah, Geert-Jan Huizing, Sohan Addagudi, Nicholas Ho, Euxhen Hasanaj, Merel Kuijs, Toby Johnstone et al. "Foundation models improve perturbation response prediction." BioRxiv (2026): 2026-02.

resources.title: From Equations to Agents: The Artificial Intelligence Virtual Cell Reshaping Precision Oncology
resources.citation: Wei, Ruochen, Boquan Wang, Bin Yan, Yuxi Yang, Wanyi Liu, Jia Ding, Dehua Hu et al. "From Equations to Agents: The Artificial Intelligence Virtual Cell Reshaping Precision Oncology." The Innovation Oncology 1 (2026): 100002.

resources.title: From modality-specific to compositional foundation models for cell biology
resources.key: Argues for compositional, modular foundation models that join chromatin, protein, spatial, imaging and text modalities on the way to agentic virtual cells.
resources.citation: Bahrami, Mojtaba, Till Richter, Niklas A. Schmacke, Aitana Egea Lavandera, and Fabian J. Theis. "From modality-specific to compositional foundation models for cell biology." Cell Systems 17, no. 2 (2026): 101534.

resources.title: Genetic Perturbation Prediction Models Fail Out-of-Distribution: A Rigorous Benchmark and Systematic Evaluation
resources.key: EL-PERTURB: stress-tests 20 perturbation models under stratified out-of-distribution splits on essential-gene and genome-wide screens.
resources.findings: Performance drops sharply out of distribution, and complexity, including foundation-model embeddings, gives no reliable advantage.
resources.citation: Tiwari, Kanupriya, Gaurang Mahajan, Renuka Prakash Bellad, Nobal Kishor Dhruw, and Abhishek K Jha. "Genetic Perturbation Prediction Models Fail Out-of-Distribution: A Rigorous Benchmark and Systematic Evaluation." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: Harmonised benchmarking of foundation models for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals context-dependent generalisation
resources.key: Harmonised benchmark of six single-cell and spatial foundation models across scRNA-seq, spatial and Perturb-seq tasks.
resources.findings: No model dominates: cell-level transformers lead identity tasks, spatial models preserve tissue structure, and language-derived gene embeddings compete on some perturbation metrics.
resources.citation: Chen, Sally, Roxana Zahedi, Lucy Chhuo, Ricky Nguyen, Marjan BaghGolshani, Amin Beheshti, Mark Grosser et al. "Harmonised benchmarking of foundation models for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals context-dependent generalisation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17227 (2026).

resources.title: How different AI models understand cells differently
resources.key: scGeneLens: sparsifies attention, propagates it across layers and applies integrated gradients to see which gene relations scFoundation and scGPT rely on.
resources.findings: scFoundation leans on cell-type marker relations (sharper cell-type separation), while scGPT leans on shared pathway genes (better transfer across conditions).
resources.citation: Zhao, Yubo, Duozhi Sun, Minsheng Hao, Yifan Xiong, Chen Li, Tieliang Gong, Lei Wei et al. "How different AI models understand cells differently." bioRxiv (2026).

resources.title: How Much Information Is Stored in Single-Cell Foundation Models, and How Much Can Be Extracted? A Review of Probing, Interpretability, and the Limits of Representation Readout
resources.key: Review of probing and interpretability for single-cell foundation models and of how much stored information can actually be read out.
resources.citation: Chen, Liu. "How Much Information Is Stored in Single-Cell Foundation Models, and How Much Can Be Extracted? A Review of Probing, Interpretability, and the Limits of Representation Readout." SSRN (2026).

resources.title: Human-Guided Causal Knowledge Injection for Virtual Cells
resources.key: Visual-analytics tool for exploring, validating and refining causal graphs injected into virtual cell models.
resources.citation: Wang, Pengcheng, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, You Wu, Long Wang, Feng Yu, and Kenli Li. "Human-Guided Causal Knowledge Injection for Virtual Cells." arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.08430 (2026).

resources.key: LLM4Cell: survey and taxonomy of 58 language-model and agentic systems for single-cell biology, mapped to tasks, datasets and ten evaluation dimensions.
